title: Eclipse models with periods near one day predict long dips in two ZTF dimmer candidates
abstract: We test whether short eclipses can explain apparent long events in two selected ZTF main-sequence dimmer candidates. For Gaia DR3 2178994311226359936, a fit before MJD 60000 gives a 0.99643128-day recurrence and a 2.59-hour width at half depth. With the eclipse fixed, later data give prediction scores of 0.892 in r and 0.586 in g. Thirty-two faint sampled nights span 128.6 days; the same eclipse at the actual visit times reproduces this group and two later groups. A locked ZTF phase also fits 53 earlier Gaia transits, including four faint transits, with a score of 0.976 when the G depth and baseline are fitted. Gaia helped select the source and frequency neighborhood, so this is cross-survey agreement. The previously noted candidate ZTF19adgqwvh gives a 0.99273269-day recurrence and later g and r scores of 0.882 and 0.888. We show how sampling near the same sidereal time turns hour-scale eclipses into week- or month-scale apparent events. Stricter cuts and an r-only fit retain the main result. This selected two-case test gives no contamination rate for the 81-candidate survey. A geometric eclipse fit does not prove companion masses, exclude a close blend or periodic dust, or refute direct dust evidence in Gaia20cdd. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and separate-scratch retrieval are included.
